title: Boundary-aware routing experiments and operator checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for a set of boundary-aware routing experiments, the operator verification checklist, and an initial test harness plan. Aim is to validate: 1) automated adjudication between regional pins and inferred locality, 2) safe fallback semantics when a pinned region is unavailable, and 3) telemetry signals that give sufficient evidence for audits and for customer-facing compliance claims.

Background / Why this exists:
We have a handful of on-going efforts (region pinning, pin enforcement, and sovereignty routing). Many docs focus on policy or rollout timelines; fewer focus on pragmatic experiment design and operator-verifiable evidence that we can produce in production or staging. This doc is intentionally lightweight — a lab notebook plus a checklist for oncall and operators to run sanity experiments and capture adjudication traces.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC + on-prem) and Dedicated where customer requests strict geo isolation.
- Does NOT replace legal review; this is engineering validation/ops guidance for how to show we honored region constraints.
- Must work with current routing layer: request attributes, customer pin metadata, and backend region availability signals.

Key definitions (for this doc):
- pin: explicit customer-configured region restriction (e.g., eu-west1).
- locality-signal: inferred region based on request IP, explicit request header, or enterprise identity provider region claim.
- adjudicator: policy component that reconciles pin + locality + capacity to pick a target region or fallback action.
- audit-evidence: structured trace (request id, chosen-region, decision-reasons, fallbacks, KV-cache keys) persisted to telemetry for legal/audit review.

Hypotheses to test:
1) The adjudicator can produce an unambiguous decision trace for 100% of requests when both a pin and locality-signal exist.
2) Fallback to compatible pinned variants (e.g., quantized model in another EU region) can be performed without leaking non-local data if pinned region is down and customer policy allows fallback.
3) Telemetry volume for detailed decision traces is manageable (< 1% of total request volume if sampled) and sufficient for post-incident audit.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Axis A: pin status: none | strict-pin | advisory-pin
- Axis B: locality-signal: match-pin | mismatch | missing
- Axis C: capacity: healthy | degraded | outage
- Axis D: fallback-policy: block | redirect-to-same-geo | redirect-compatible | tombstone-and-queue

For each combination we will assert: routing-decision, latency impact, evidence-recorded, and customer-visible response.

Minimal test harness plan:
1) Synthetic traffic generator (tg) that can emit requests with configurable headers, IPs, and customer pin metadata.
2) Staging fleet with region simulators to toggle capacity states and to inject controlled KV-cache miss/hit patterns.
3) Adjudication trace exporter that writes newline-delimited JSON to a staging telemetry stream (sampled).
4) Small audit viewer (not prod) that can query traces by request id and present a decision timeline.

Operator checklist (pre-experiment):
- Confirm staging environment pinned models match prod naming and have version tags.
- Load tg with small baseline (100 req/s) and verify ingress routing.
- Deploy adjudicator debug flag so it emits full decision payload to trace exporter.
- Ensure KLUDGE: sampling set to 100% for staging, but <1% for canary prod.
- Set up capacity toggles for region-sim nodes and verify via telemetry that simulated outages are visible to routing layer.

Operator checklist (during run):
- Start a single experiment row (one combination from matrix) and record start time.
- Validate decision trace for first 50 requests; look for decision-reason fields (pin-match, fallback-allowed, capacity-driven).
- Monitor error budgets and latency SLOs for affected routes. Abort if >10% increase in 95th p90 latency or error spike.
- For fallback experiments, confirm no request body or sensitive headers are routed outside allowed boundaries per policy.
- Flag anomalous decisions (e.g., chosen-region = us-east when strict-pin=eu) immediately to #eng-residency with request ids.

Observability and telemetry fields (proposal):
- trace_id (string)
- request_id (string)
- incoming_locality (string)
- customer_pin (string|null)
- adjudicated_region (string)
- decision_reasons (comma-separated string)
- fallback_policy_used (string|null)
- capacity_signal (string)
- model_variant (string)
- kv_cache_hit (true|false)
- timestamp_iso (string)
- operator_tag (string|null)

(Important: telemetry schema stored separately in Infra telemetry repo; this is a minimal surface for experiment traces.)

Sample decision-reasons taxonomy (short):
- PIN_MATCH
- LOCALITY_MATCH
- PIN_OVERRIDE (customer policy explicitly outranks locality)
- CAPACITY_FORCE_FALLBACK
- FALLBACK_NOT_ALLOWED
- NO_LOCALITY
- CHECKSUM_MISMATCH (model variant mismatch)

Audit evidence requirements (customer-facing claims we must be able to support):
- For any request within a pinned region window, provide a trace showing adjudicated_region = pinned-region and reason includes PIN_MATCH.
- For fallbacks, provide evidence that the fallback policy was honored and that data residency boundaries were not violated (e.g., payload not forwarded to an unrestricted region).

Open questions & risk notes (explicit):
- Q: Can pinned-region metadata be modified mid-request by proxies? Risk: trust boundary with customer-managed ingress.
- Q: How to handle multi-tenant requests where different parts of a request have different residency constraints? Risk: policy complexity may require per-subrequest routing.
- Risk: High-fidelity traces increase telemetry costs and may contain sensitive metadata; need a retention and redaction policy.
- Q: Will legal accept sampling (we currently propose 1% sampling in prod) for audit purposes? Action: ask Legal and CS to sign off on sampling thresholds.

Playbook snippets (for specific scenarios):
- Scenario: pinned-region=EU, capacity outage in EU node cluster.
  Action: if fallback-policy==block -> return 403 with standard error code RESIDENCY_BLOCKED and include request_id and operator_contact. If fallback-policy==redirect-compatible -> route to eu-2 (compatible variant) and include audit tag FALLBACK_COMPAT.

- Scenario: no pin, locality mismatch (ip claims US but idp claims EU).
  Action: adjudicator uses policy precedence (IDP > IP) and annotates trace with LOCALITY_IDP, and customer-visible headers show chosen-region.

- Scenario: advisory-pin (customer requested preference but allowed fallback).
  Action: simulate both choices in staging (respect and override) and compare quality regressions; propose default=respect but allow explicit override with admin approval.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Implement adjudicator debug export in staging (ticket JIRA-PLAT-1392) — owners: Maya / Liam.
2) Build tg scenario templates and share them in /repos/test-harness/scenarios/boundary-routing — owner: Diego.
3) Legal and CS review for sampling / retention (request ticket to Legal) — owner: Sana.
4) Run a two-week sandpit of experiments and capture representative traces; produce short report and example evidence bundle.

Notes to self (loose):
- When we run in prod canary, ensure fallback decisions are throttled and can be rolled back via runtime flag.
- Keep sample viewer simple: a filtered tail view by request id with expandable decision-reason list.
- Link to existing residency policy doc in Confluence in the final report.

References and related:
- Confluence: region-routing-overview (linked above)
- PR: platform/routing#4278 (adjudicator refactor)
- Previous runbook: residency-enforcement-testing-corpus-and-runbook (search Drive for earlier runs)

End of note.
